regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: Kirkwood leads with 50" over the week, peaking at 26" Wednesday. Heavy snow is forecast Wednesday and Wednesday night. A Winter Storm Watch runs Tuesday night through Friday. Palisades (38") and Sierra-at-Tahoe (36") are close behind.

regions.title: Eastern Sierra
regions.text: Mammoth gets 38" over the week, peaking at 22" Wednesday. Expect strong southwest wind with gusts to 60 mph Wednesday night. The NWS is calling for more, 34" to 57" Monday through Friday. A Winter Storm Watch runs Wednesday through Friday.

regions.title: Wasatch
regions.text: Powder Mountain, Snowbird and Alta are all in the 12" to 13" range, with Tuesday the biggest day at 7". The NWS is calling for more at Powder Mountain (20" to 36") and Snowbird (25" to 45") Tuesday through Friday night. Snow levels could drop near 5,000 feet Friday night.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: Grand Targhee leads at 12", with snow showers Tuesday and Friday. Sun Valley (10") and Jackson Hole (9") bring light to moderate snow showers across the week. The NWS is calling for more at Grand Targhee, 9" to 21" Tuesday through Friday night.

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: Steamboat tops the region at 9", but most of it is due Friday, when 8" is forecast. Tuesday brings rain mixed with snow at Steamboat. Telluride (8") and Crested Butte (7") see their snow mostly Tuesday and Friday.

regions.title: Southern Rockies
regions.text: Wolf Creek leads with 14", peaking at 8" Tuesday. Gusts to 60 mph are forecast Tuesday night, so expect rough lift conditions. The NWS is calling for more at Wolf Creek, 16" to 32" Tuesday through Friday night. Taos sees only 2" over the week.

ahead.text: The Weather Prediction Center expects a Pacific atmospheric river to bring heavy mountain snow to California around Wednesday Nov 25. Confidence in the timing and track is moderate, since model runs still disagree on the storm's speed.
